newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sugar eases further, Dec/March eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sugar eases further, Dec/March eases.

text.p: LIFFE white sugar futures racked up losses on Tuesday afternoon with activity centred on routine trade-related business in Dec/March switches.

The spread was bid at $1 and offered at $1.50 after trading at $1.50 in the afternoon. Earlier trades were clinched at $2.00. "It's all centred around the December expiry. People are getting out of their December longs," said one trader.
A total turnover of 3,400 lots by 1630 GMT was said to have included over 700 lots of switches, mainly Dec/March.
The key December contract shed $1.60 on the day to $306.10 a tonne, after a session low of $305.90. Traders pegged psychological support at $300.00 but technical help could come around $305.00.
They said the market was debilitated by lack of significant offtake despite the recent fall in prices.

"We're talking about standard offtake," said one trader, adding that big buyers like Russia and China were absent. In other news, the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) revised its 1996 sugar beat harvest forecast up by 1.4 percent to 4.38 million tonnes.
Poland said it would buy an undisclosed amount of sugar from the country's expected 400,000 tonne production surplus this year for state reserves.
New York contracts were narrowly mixed while in Paris, March sugar traded at $304.50 a tonne, down $1.50 from Monday.
